title: In the 1980s, Scotland planted commercial trees across parts of a 9,000-year-old peatland
summary_full: The ancient peatlands of Scotland are undergoing a significant restoration, which addresses the detrimental effects caused by tree planting. Conservationists are diligently working to eliminate commercial trees, aiming to enhance wildlife habitats and maintain stored carbon levels. This notable effort is primarily focused on the Flow Country, a treasure trove of wetlands recognized as a World Heritage Site for its global ecological importance.
